knowledgeGraph.headingContext: Properties of Lines Perpendicular to Planes

question: What relationship between two lines is the conclusion of the property theorem?
solution:
The standalone stem does not identify the property theorem. For example, the tangent property theorem concludes that a tangent is perpendicular to the line containing the radius to the point of tangency, which would give A.

If the reported heading, “Properties of Lines Perpendicular to Planes,” identifies the intended theorem, the two lines are distinct and perpendicular to the same plane. Both lines being perpendicular to the same plane implies that they are parallel. Thus the answer is B, Parallel, under that interpretation; the standalone stem alone does not determine a unique choice.

Coplanarity uses what a plane is and how points and lines determine one.
The property assumes lines perpendicular to the plane.
edges.scope: two lines perpendicular to one plane

edges.reason: Retain requires, narrowly for recognizing the line and plane objects used in the definition. cnm_052 explicitly concerns the geometric components point/line/surface/solid. Its motion-generation illustration is not demanded by this edge; dropping the shared primitive meanings because of that extra content would confuse scoped content necessity with mastery of the whole prerequisite lesson.

The spatial definition extends perpendicular line directions; skew supporting lines may be compared using parallels. The target presupposes meanings of lines, planes and perpendicular directions. It does not require the full motion-generation picture from cnm_052, nor can the two-intersecting-lines theorem replace the all-directions definition.
